SEE ALSO: Who could replace Jensen Huang at Nvidia long-term? Here are the top contenders. The AI boom has sparked a significant spike in demand for computer components, leading to increasing profits for chipmakers such as Nvidia. Earlier this year, the company reported $81.6 billion in revenue during Q1 and $96.2 billion in Q2 . This growth has continued in Q4, with Nvidia announcing its quarterly revenue had increased by 20 percent to $115.8 billion. However, the elephant in the room was Huang, whose recent scandal and departure prompted a significant drop in Nvidia's stock . During Tuesday's earnings call, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones stated that Huang had voluntarily resigned on Nov. 12 "after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms." Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO , with CFO Colette Kress acting in the role in the interim. body: If you like playing daily word games like Wordle , then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine. There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown. An important note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle. title: Only Murders in the Building Season 6 trailer goes to London
body: Only Murders in the Building 's Season 6 trailer is here, and the podcasters have well and truly left the building. Renamed Only Murders in London , Hulu 's comedy mystery is headed across the pond for its sixth season, with Charles (Steve Martin), Oliver (Martin Short) , and Mabel ( Selena Gomez ) hoping to discover what happened to their latest true crime podcast subject. Season 5 ended with the death of fellow podcaster Cinda Canning ( Tina Fey ), who was found at the gate of the titular Arconia apartment building. Determined to investigate, Only Murders in the Building 's intrepid crime-solving trio are now headed to London, the location of Canning's last podcast episode. Judging from the trailer, it seems as though they'll quickly encounter more than one culture clash as well as a smorgasbord of very European characters. The star-studded lineup of actors joining Season 6 includes Nicola Coughlan , Olivia Colman , Martin Freeman , Richard E. Grant , Jim Broadbent , former Spice Girl Geri Halliwell-Horner, and even Doctor Who 's Tenth, Twelfth, and Thirteenth Doctors David Tennant , Peter Capaldi , and Jodie Whittaker . title: FAA official oversaw router work just before nationwide ground stop, report claims
body: An official with the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) was on the ground in Arkansas when new telecommunications wires were replaced, an action that preceded Friday's national ground stop by eight minutes, according to the Washington Post . The FAA official oversaw the work, tested it, and signed off on it, according to the Post 's report. The work involved replacing a router and swapping old copper wires for new fiber-optic cables, part of a national effort by the FAA to upgrade the airline industry's communication infrastructure. SEE ALSO: Apple confirms iCloud sign-in issues, App Store and Apple Pay outages The fact that an FAA official greenlit the work complicates Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy's efforts to point fingers at L3Harris Technologies, a tech services provider and contractor tasked with updating the wires in Arkansas and leading the FAA's fiber-optic upgrades. Duffy said on Saturday that his agency is looking into whether "incompetence" by L3Harris led to the 4.5-hour ground stop. Responding to the Post 's request for comment, the FAA pointed to statements Duffy made on Tuesday in a news conference at the Capitol. During the conference, Duffy said that he wanted L3Harris to "hire better minds" for the wire replacement work and was considering bringing in new contractors to help. An exact cause for the communications outage has not yet been confirmed, an anonymous source told the Post . Duffy told reporters on Saturday that the replaced router in Arkansas was faulty and flooded the network with over 1,000 connection attempts every few seconds ,

title: Copilot is "the new OS for work," and now Office runs inside of it
author: Nick Indge
body: Opening the keynote at its Ignite event, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella outlined the company's vision for its new "frontier ecosystem," announcing Tuesday the general availability of Word, Excel, and PowerPoint inside Copilot, which he described as "the new OS for work." The announcement is a striking inversion of how we've traditionally used software. Rather than an app like Word being the attraction and Clippy the assistant to help you use it, Microsoft envisions the new Copilot integrations will see agents driving things, with the software packages riding shotgun. Applications will become plugin components of the agent's work, backed by an organizational knowledge layer that draws context from emails, meetings, calendars, chats, and files. Users will now be able to create documents, spreadsheets, and presentations directly in Copilot, with the resulting files remaining editable in their respective Office applications. SEE ALSO: California sues OpenAI for being a 'public nuisance' Frist reported by the San Francisco Business Times , the California DMV issued a notice on Nov. 11 that a small number of Waymo vehicles in the San Francisco Bay Area had entered restricted construction zones on U.S. Route 101 despite notice of closures. Another vehicle reportedly impeded California Highway Patrol on Highway 280. Because of these "recurring incursions," the state announced it would ban self-driving taxis from state freeways until the company implemented "effective corrective actions," the DMV said in a statement to TechCrunch. The department called the incidents an imminent hazard to public safety. Waymo, which is owned by Google's parent holding company, Alphabet, responded by pausing freeway access for its entire nationwide fleet. Freeways had been accessible to Waymo cabs in select cities since 2025, with a brief, unexplained pause from May to July of this year. title: Yet another satellite company is jockeying for a rocket—but this one makes sense
author: Stephen Clark
body: Finnish satellite developer ICEYE announced Tuesday that it is seeking to buy Italian rocket-maker Avio for more than $2.2 billion in a transaction aimed at creating Europe's first true vertically integrated end-to-end space company. The announcement came as an all-cash voluntary tender offer from an Italian subsidiary of ICEYE to Avio's shareholders, led by the Italian defense conglomerate Leonardo. Avio said its board of directors "has taken note of the notice" from ICEYE and is considering the purchase offer. Avio builds the Vega C rocket, a solid-fueled launcher designed to carry up to 3.3 metric tons (7,300 pounds) of payload to low-Earth orbit. The Vega C has flown successfully seven times in eight attempts since 2022. It is a follow-on to an earlier version of the Vega rocket that amassed a 20-for-22 record since debuting in 2012. title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
author: Dan Goodin
body: Hundreds of websites using the Optimizely website personalization platform served unsuspecting visitors a potent malware cocktail that targeted cryptocurrency wallets, stole payment card data, cookies, and screenshots, and delivered exploit kits for infecting iPhones and iPads, researchers said Tuesday. ReportURI said it identified 178 websites—including CNN, Zoom, the BBC, and Salesforce—that were affected. JavaScript digitally signed by Optimizely and then loaded into customer pages had been modified to include malicious components that attempted to infect visitor devices with multiple payloads. When wares were installed successfully, they swapped user cryptocurrency wallet addresses for the attackers. Other components skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and, on iPhones and iPads, delivered iOS exploit kits known as Coruna and DarkSword. Optimizely infrastructure delivers multipurpose malware Optimizely serves JavaScript “snippets” that include both company code and code that is provided by each customer. The JavaScript, which can be served directly from Optimizely or from a customer endpoint, runs on every page the customer serves. Somehow, the attackers wrote their own code into a portion of each affected customer’s JavaScript and then delivered it from cdn.optimizely.com. A valid certificate for that domain signed the JavaScript. Read full article Comments

title: Are the recent outages connected? What we know.
body: Microsoft 365, including Outlook, goes down for two days starting on Nov. 12. The FAA grounds all U.S. flights due to an air traffic control telecommunications issue on Nov. 13. Chase bank suffers an outage due to a software issue on Nov. 16. Later that same day, United Airlines ' website goes down, affecting all departing flights. On Nov. 17, an internal update issue disrupted some of Apple's services . Major companies and services appear to be experiencing outages all at the same time. Conspiracy theories surrounding these events are spreading, and people are asking what in the world is going on with all these recent outages and are they connected? Some answers on the outages It indeed appears there have been an unusually high number of outages recently. "Compared with the past 12 months, the past week has been unusually busy," Ookla's Lead Industry Analyst Luke Kehoe said in a statement provided to Mashable. "Americans sent nearly 6 million reports in the past seven days to November 16, more than in any other week over that period, and the number of services with problems flagged on Downdetector was higher than in all but a few weeks." According to Ookla, the two-day Microsoft 365 outage was the largest reported downtime issue on Downdetector "since the AWS outage of October 2025, with 3.9 million US reports in the 60 hours after it began." However, the reason it feels like outages have occurred more frequently is that the affected companies have been fairly large. title: Instagram takes on AI copycat videos once and for all
body: As AI tools have gotten better at transforming videos, social media creators have faced a growing wave of accounts copying their work. From influencers watching their videos reappear with a different face, to comedians finding their jokes delivered by fictional performers, the copies can preserve the original creator's material while sending the attention elsewhere. ( Read Mashable's feature on this phenomenon here. ) SEE ALSO: Fake influencers, real money: Inside the AI creator business Now, Instagram is introducing tools to help creators catch those copies and decide what happens next. On Tuesday, Nov. 17, Instagram head Adam Mosseri announced that the platform is beginning to roll out "Content Protection," as a "new way to see and review copies of your own videos in your insights on Instagram," giving creators the choice whether to hide them or add a link back to the original. Separately, Instagram is testing a way to detect stolen scripts and jokes, even when someone uses AI to change the visuals. "We will not get everything right at first, but we ll keep improving as fast as we can. More to come," he wrote on Threads. For now, the feature remains a limited test with a small number of creators, a Meta spokesperson told The Hollywood Reporter , with plans to expand access. Mashable has reached out for a comment. The distinction matters for creators whose work has been repackaged this way, especially comedians like Sarah Purdum , who told Mashable in October that her material had been used by an AI account. title: TikTok creators are joining Disney+ as Hulu integration wraps up
body: Disney fans have spent years turning their favorite movies and shows into TikTok videos. Starting in December, some of those videos will have a place on Disney+ itself. Disney shared the timing in its fiscal fourth-quarter earnings announcement on Nov. 17, saying the rollout will coincide with the buildup to Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday , which opens in theaters Dec. 18. The launch gives a date to the content-sharing partnership Disney and TikTok first announced in August, which lets participating creators make short videos using material from Disney's movies and series. It's also another sign of how closely streaming services are watching the creator economy. How will TikTok videos work on Disney+? The videos will appear in Verts , the vertical video feed Disney+ launched in its U.S. mobile app in March. Subscribers can already swipe through scenes from movies and shows, save titles to their Watchlist, or start watching the full thing. The TikTok partnership will bring creators' own takes on Disney stories into that mix. The invite-only program is "designed for passionate fans who already make content around Disney IP on TikTok," according to Disney's program page . Invitations are rolling out beginning in November, with selected videos from participating creators appearing on both platforms. The agreement covers brands including Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars , and FX, starting with a U.S. pilot before expanding into other markets. (Disney hasn't announced an exact December launch date.) There is technically another way that we'll cover in a little while, but for all intents and purposes, you cannot have the same experience everyone else is having without buying a PS5 or Xbox Series console. We don't know this yet for sure, but there's a possibility that GTA 6 is an incredible video game. You probably wouldn't want to miss out on that. What are you going to do while everyone else is having an amazing time parading through Leonida, read books? Come on, that sounds boring. One thing that's also worth remembering is that other video games exist. A lot of them, in fact. FEMA will also conduct a scheduled test of the emergency alert system on Tuesday afternoon, adding to the sense of generalized anxiety. title: OpenAI sued by California after admitting to 80 loss-of-control incidents
author: Jon Brodkin
body: California sued OpenAI yesterday, alleging it has tried to evade responsibility for the Hugging Face attack and about 80 other incidents in which the company lost control of its AI. The lawsuit was filed under the state's public nuisance and unfair competition laws. The July 2026 hack of Hugging Face and other attacks carried out by OpenAI's autonomous agents "may just be the tip of the iceberg," said a lawsuit filed in a state court by California Attorney General Rob Bonta. "OpenAI recently admitted to the Attorney General’s Office that it has lost control of its autonomous AI agents over 80 times during testing." OpenAI had publicly reported only 27 such incidents, showing that "OpenAI’s public reports do not represent the full scope of loss-of-control incidents involving OpenAI’s models that have impacted third parties," the lawsuit said. OpenAI "knowingly tested a dangerous product without proper oversight or safety procedures and misled the public about it," Bonta said in a press release . Read full article Comments

title: FEMA is testing the emergency alert system: Dont panic
body: If you hear an emergency broadcast this afternoon, don't panic! The Federal Emergency Management Agency ( FEMA ) and the Federal Communications Commission ( FCC ) are conducting a scheduled test of the national emergency alert system at 2:20 p.m. ET on Tuesday, Nov. 17. The FCC released a public notice about the scheduled test on Sept. 16, but it comes at a moment of high national anxiety, driven by recent tech outages among other troubling news stories. First, Microsoft suffered a widespread global outage on Thursday, Nov. 12, followed by a rare FAA nationwide ground stoppage the following day. And on Monday, a JPMorgan Chase outage sparked reports of a major bank outage (the problem was limited to Chase Bank and not a systemic issue or the result of a cyberattack), followed quickly by a United Airlines outage . None of these outages were directly related to or caused by cyberattackers, but the timing has sparked conspiracy theories and generalized anxiety. SEE ALSO: Trump says he takes 'no responsibility' for nationwide FAA ground stop However, the emergency alert was scheduled long before these outages; the FCC also announced a backup date of Dec. 3, in the event today's test does not occur. So, if your TV or radio suddenly goes into emergency mode today, don't freak out. FEMA will use the Integrated Public Alert and Warning System (IPAWS) to disseminate a message in both English and Spanish. title: Google makes it easier to use Gemini without training AI on your data
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: It can be hard to use Google products—or even the Internet itself—without coming into contact with Gemini AI. That is, of course, by design . The more you use Gemini, the more data Google collects to train and improve its generative AI chatbot. The options to limit training on your data have been scant, but Google is finally adding more controls to the Gemini app. The change currently rolling out to Gemini will separate your chat history from training, which allows you to retain basic AI functionality without handing Google quite so much control over your data. Prior to this change, the only way to opt out of contributing your chat contents (including attachments) for training was to turn off your history. That made it impossible to go back and pick up a chat down the road. As the new settings roll out, users will see separate toggles for model training and chat history. The history setting will continue to support an adjustable limit, but you will no longer have to change it to stop Google from training on your Gemini usage. Meanwhile, AI training will be an opt-out situation. You'll need to find the toggle to block Google from using your chats for AI training. It's under Activity in the Gemini settings. You can also access the menu from your Google account under Data and Privacy My Activity Other activity Gemini Apps Activity. Read full article Comments

According to the statement, U.S. agencies opened an investigation into Megaspeed in 2024 for "potential export control violations" after noticing suspicious activity. The Department of Commerce requested records from Nvidia regarding sales to Megaspeed in May 2025. (The export of advanced AI chips is highly regulated to protect national security, and Nvidia makes many of the chips that power the U.S. AI industry.) One month later, Nvidia put Megaspeed on its "no sell" list. That same month, U.S. agents and Singaporean law enforcement conducted an in-person investigation at Megaspeed and interviewed Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang. Following this on-site action, the Department of Justice "took the lead role in the criminal investigation of Megaspeed," according to the statement. "While we don t typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting," the joint statement says. Last week, Nvidia cofounder and CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company after he admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, who U.S. Intelligence alleges is a spy for the Chinese government. title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
author: Dan Goodin
body: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with. In some cases, the unapproved access attempts occurred while the laptop with Grok Bot installed had its lid shut, or late at night while the employee was sleeping. None of the unprompted actions were recorded in Grok logs. Without the gateway logs, the employees would have had no idea they occurred. And of course, without the gateway, the unapproved accesses would have succeeded—again without the end user's knowledge. It’s “worse than a bug” Once the employees learned that Grok Bot had tried to check in with accounts without prompting, one of them instructed the agent, four separate times, to stop taking any actions on its own. The agent's reply was: “I won’t set that up, and I’ll stop offering recurring check-ins.” Despite acknowledging the explicit instructions, the Grok Bot made more unapproved access attempts. title: Sunrise on the Reaping review: The biggest and boldest Hunger Games yet
body: Are you looking for a movie to thoroughly wallop you? To leave you emotionally battered, physically exhausted, and full of despair and hope at the same time? Then allow me to prescribe a healthy dose of The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping , the sixth film in the Hunger Games series. Based on Suzanne Collins' second prequel novel following The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes , Sunrise on the Reaping once again rewinds the clock on Panem to the 50th Hunger Games, otherwise known as the Second Quarter Quell. These are the biggest Hunger Games yet, with 48 tributes instead of the standard 24. Among them is Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada), future mentor to series protagonists Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark. SEE ALSO: The first 20 minutes of 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' blew me away The question here is not whether Haymitch will survive the games. We know, by virtue of the entire original trilogy, that he does. But before he was the cynical, heavy-drinking, lone wolf victor audiences met in The Hunger Games , he was an optimistic 16-year-old with a caring family, a loving relationship, and a solid community in District 12. So the real question of Sunrise on the Reaping becomes, what broke that young man down so thoroughly? The answer is, unsurprisingly, bleak as all hell. But director Francis Lawrence executes it in thrilling (if occasionally overstuffed) fashion, with a Hunger Games sequence that blows series-high Catching Fire 's own games out of the water, and a dogged focus on the philosophical themes at the core of Collins' work. title: Oura launches Jet Lag Plan, letting users hack their travel
body: Oura Ring users who are always on the go are about to benefit from a feature to combat jet lag. Jet Lag Plan is a new Oura feature that creates a plan to navigate time changes before, during, and after travel. We have all been there with travel. As much fun as the vacation is, if you're dealing with time zone changes, jet lag can totally kill the vibe. You don't want to waste a moment in a new place by taking a nap back at the hotel. Oura wants to help its Oura Ring users combat jet lag with its latest feature. The new feature is built off of a National University of Singapore study that used 1.5 million nights of sleep data from de-identified Oura users. Jet Lag Plan builds a plan designed just for you. It uses your flight itinerary along with your sleep patterns and chronotype to craft a series of recommendations. It produces a personalized schedule around sleep, light exposure, activity, and caffeine for journeys that cross three or more time zones. The feature uses Oura's AI-powered support, Oura Advisor, to adjust the plan as travel changes, in case things don't go as expected. Jet Lag Plan will be available globally to users with Gen 3 or newer hardware on both iOS and Android, as long as users have their language set to English. So if you're traveling for the holidays, don't let jet lag stop you from your vacation or family time. Opens in a new window Credit: Oura Oura Ring 5 $399 at Amazon Shop Now at Amazon

title: California sues OpenAI for being a public nuisance
body: California is suing OpenAI , accusing ChatGPT 's creator of endangering the public by knowingly developing AI models without appropriate safeguards. It also alleges that the AI company constitutes a "public nuisance" under local law. SEE ALSO: OpenAI launches tool for finding child sexual abuse material Filed to the Superior Court of California on Monday , the lawsuit accuses OpenAI of violating California's unfair competition laws by engaging in "unlawful, unfair, or fraudulent acts or practices." Such alleged acts include making statements misleading people into believing OpenAI develops its AI models safely and responsibly, and testing said models without adequate security measures in place to protect the public. This lawsuit follows an incident in July where an OpenAI agent escaped its testing environment and hacked Hugging Face , an open-source repository of AI models, datasets, and tools. "The Hugging Face attack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability and this was only one of 80 known incidents," California Attorney General Rob Bonta said in a press release. The filing cited several of these incidents, including a breach in June where an OpenAI agent hacked the Australian government's healthcare system . Researchers have previously identified multiple instances of AI models escaping and hacking external organisations, including some created by OpenAI. title: Three small failures combined to take down Microsoft 365
author: Nick Indge
body: A hidden defect in Microsoft's cloud gateway, dormant since July, was to blame for one of the largest outages in the company's history last week. A preliminary Post-Incident Report (PIR) released by the company outlines how the latent bug, changes in traffic, and reduced server capacity combined to knock much of Microsoft 365 and Exchange infrastructure offline at the end of last week. Microsoft's report lists the incident's final status as "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents." Microsoft's preliminary report places the outage between November 12 at 16:20 UTC and November 13 at 16:10 UTC, just under 24 hours total, and additional monitoring remained in place for any affected systems through November 14. The outage started on November 12 and quickly rippled through businesses and public offices that depend on Microsoft's cloud and email exchange infrastructure. The outage is covered in Microsoft's incident IDs EX1550543 and MO1550821. You need Microsoft 365 admin credentials to see the full report on the company's status pages, but Office Watch has reproduced the preliminary report , and the University of Pennsylvania maintains an archive of Microsoft's service-health updates . title: OpenAI launches tool for finding child sexual abuse material
body: OpenAI announced Monday the release of a new tool to detect child sexual abuse material (CSAM), including content generated by artificial intelligence . The tool is a classifier that looks for visual signs of abuse in images. It then scores images to help human reviewers prioritize which of them warrant attention. OpenAI said its CSAM classifier is the first broadly available tool of its kind to include a specific signal indicating the image may be generated with AI. This capability is becoming critical as AI-generated CSAM skyrockets. A new analysis conducted by Childlight Global Child Safety Institute at the University of Edinburgh found AI-related reports of CSAM increased globally by more than 8,400 percent from 2023 to 2025. Last year, the National Center for Missing Exploited Children received more than 400,000 of these reports. In 2023, that number was roughly 4,700. SEE ALSO: How AI child sexual abuse material is colliding with free speech protections "Individual companies like OpenAI have a responsibility to prevent our technology from being exploited by predators to harm children, and we also must work together with the broader industry, child safety organizations and law enforcement to advance our collective efforts to protect children online," OpenAI said in its blog post about the announcement. The company's new tool can be used by organizations required or authorized to detect CSAM, including certain developers that use OpenAI's application programming interface, or API. title: How long it takes to play GTA 6: Playthrough and achievements
body: Grand Theft Auto VI is almost here. The highly anticipated video game will finally come out in the U.S. on Nov. 19, more than 13 years after its predecessor. SEE ALSO: 'GTA 6': 3 intriguing new details we just learned If you patiently waited more than a decade for GTA 6, you're probably hoping for a long, immersive experience that makes it worth the wait. Good news! Reports are now coming in from game reviewers, and it seems like you're in for a treat. You'll likely be playing GTA 6 for a long time. According to Insider Gaming , GTA 6 will take around 50 hours to complete the main campaign. That estimate covers nearly 100 missions across the five chapters of the game. Of course, your playtime may vary depending on your skill level. But, that seems to be the average based on reports. However, that's just the amount of time to complete GTA 6's main campaign. If you want to fully complete everything in the game, you're looking at a much longer gameplay time. Much longer. Aside from GTA 6's main campaign, there are also side quests and an array of interactions, events, and locations to explore. Gamers will likely want to unlock the reported 55 achievements, including the Platinum Trophy and the Mythic achievement. If you want to do all of that, you're looking at a reported 200 hours of gameplay for GTA 6. That's not even counting any time spent just wandering the streets of Vice City or cruising around in a car while listening to the stacked GTA 6 soundtrack . So, lock in, gamers (and please take plenty of breaks). More than 200 hours of GTA 6 await.

title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
author: Scott K. Johnson
body: One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built. A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward. Finding the centers The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts. Read full article Comments

title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place

body: On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration's purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government's actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications. The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision. The suit was initially filed by a large group of researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and UC San Francisco, contesting grants originally issued by many federal agencies, from the National Institutes of Health to the Department of Transportation. At issue were grants that had been terminated because the agencies decided they violated a Trump executive order blocking the use of DEI. title: When will humans actually fly on Starship?
author: Eric Berger
body: The stunning return of Starship from the skies to a launch tower in South Texas answered some questions about the future of SpaceX's ambitious rocket program. Namely, it is now rapidly moving toward rapidly reusable launch. However, it raises other questions. For example, as Starship becomes fully reusable, when might humans fly on the vehicle? The short answer is pretty simple: If SpaceX prioritizes human spaceflight on Starship, it could happen reasonably quickly. The longer answer becomes more complicated and depends on what one means by human spaceflight. The first people to fly on Starship probably won't launch from Earth, or land here. Rather, they will probably be NASA's lunar astronauts. So there are different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth. Read full article Comments

title: What is vibe manufacturing? AI projects are leaving the chat
body: The next wave of AI projects might just arrive in the mail. As AI tools become more capable, people are asking chatbots to help design things they can hold, wear, or install in their homes, from custom jewelry and household gadgets to metal parts built around precise measurements. Welcome to " vibe manufacturing ." The phrase borrows from " vibe coding ," where people describe the software they want and ask AI to help create it. Here, the goal is a physical object, with AI helping develop a design that can be printed at home or sent to a manufacturer. The appeal is easy to understand. Most people have encountered a product that would be perfect if it were a little smaller, worked differently, or fit that one awkward space. These tools offer a starting point for making their own version. Getting it right, though, still takes more than a good prompt. SEE ALSO: What is vibe coding? Plus 7 AI coding tools to get started right away. What is vibe manufacturing? Vibe manufacturing loosely describes using conversational AI to help design and build physical things. Someone explains what they want, supplies measurements or reference images, and works with an AI tool to develop it. Depending on the project, that could involve generating a digital model, choosing components, writing software for a device, or figuring out assembly. The bridge between the conversation and the object is often CAD, short for computer-aided design . title: Microsoft outage cause revealed: It was a perfect storm of problems
body: You're probably aware that Microsoft 365, the popular suite of products that includes Outlook, suffered a massive global outage last week. In fact, it was the worst outage of the year , by a sizable margin. The problem took the computer giant roughly 24 hours, over the course of two business days , to get everything back up and running. Aside from wondering when their email would be working again , the number one question on everyone's mind was what in the world happened to keep Microsoft 365 down for so long? Now, we know. In a statement shared with customers and on X, Microsoft explained there were actually three causes, which created a perfect storm. First, a bug caused servers to become unresponsive in specific conditions; second, an issue with Microsoft Teams increased server traffic and created those conditions; and third, many additional servers were already offline from an unrelated issue. As Microsoft explained, on their own, neither issue would have caused such a large-scale problem. However, together, well, they kept one of the world's biggest tech companies scrambling for two days to fix their service. title: US now "comfortable" with children dying of measles as death toll hits 10
author: Beth Mole
body: Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania , one in New York , and one in Wisconsin . Wisconsin health officials said the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania's health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state's seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County , but state health officials have not confirmed it. For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they're the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania's case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650. Read full article Comments

title: Its official: Robert Pattinson is our new James Bond
body: Martinis are flowing from the chimneys at Pinewood Studios, which can only mean one thing: We have our new James Bond. On Nov. 16, Amazon MGM Studios announced that the newest 007 will be Robert Pattinson. He takes over the role from Daniel Craig, whose last film was 2021's No Time to Die . The next Bond film, the franchise's 26th, will be helmed by Dune director Denis Villeneuve. Pattinson has also worked with Villeneuve on Dune: Part Three . View this post on Instagram Aside from the Bond announcement, 2026 has been a banner year for Pattinson. He topped the box office with The Odyssey and cemented himself as an A24 darling with roles in The Drama and Primetime . While Pattinson has starred in smaller, stranger indie projects, he has also developed a seemingly paradoxical reputation as a franchise man. He is Batman, after all, with The Batman: Part II set for a Feb. 18, 2028 release. Before Pattinson became Battinson, moody eyeshadow and all, he captured hearts as Edward Cullen in the Twilight franchise, as well as Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter . Plus, while not part of a franchise, his role as agent Neil in Christopher Nolan's Tenet proved he's got the chops to play a suave agent. Other contenders for film's most famous spy included Slow Horses ' Jack Lowden, One Night Only 's Callum Turner, Challengers ' Josh O'Connor, and Superman 's Nicholas Hoult, all of whom reportedly screen tested for the role. Frankenstein 's Jacob Elordi and Sinners ' Jack O'Connell were reportedly in the running as well, although did not end up screen testing.

SAN FRANCISCO—When Ars first drove the new Mercedes-Benz CLA last year , the automaker also gave us a sneak preview of its next driver assist. Called Drive Assist Pro, it’s for collaborative partially assisted driving, and from the passenger seat at the time, the demo was impressive . While most automakers want a reputation for safety, Mercedes has long used passive and active technology to do so in its products. It was one of the first OEMs to introduce airbags, and a decade later started adding active safety systems like anti-lock brakes, electronic stability control, and adaptive cruise control. And so, by giving the car’s electronics the ability to control the brakes and throttle, we arrive at the first level of assisted driving—called “level 1” in automotive engineer-speak. “Level 2” assisted driving, where the car also controls the steering as well as the acceleration and braking, got famous with Tesla Autopilot. But the first lane-keeping assists predate it by almost a decade in passenger cars, when Toyota introduced a system in 2004. title: Delivery drones are coming. For some with PTSD, that's a terrifying prospect.
author: Sean Gallagher
body: In August, Amazon announced plans to expand its Prime Air delivery drone program to “ nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026 ." Combined with similar uncrewed aerial delivery programs from DoorDash and Zipline (in partnership with Uber and Walmart), the expansion suggests that flying robots dropping their payloads onto suburban lawns will soon be commonplace. For many people, delivery drones will be little more than a novelty, occasionally good for a laugh when one does something ridiculous. For others, though, their growing use could be a nightmare. As the instant delivery industry clears the last FAA hurdles to rapid deliveries beyond an operator's line of sight, an increasing number of people worldwide are living with post-traumatic stress disorder or other anxiety-related disorders triggered by drones. The use of all manner of weaponized drones in the ongoing war in Ukraine and in Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Gaza has already produced an epidemic of what some mental health professionals have dubbed “dronophobia. ” And while relatively few US troops have been targeted by drones flown by Iran, ISIS, and Iran-backed militias throughout the Middle East, even those who have not directly been attacked may experience anxiety simply because of the ample video footage of attacks circulating in news and social media. title: SNLs Sister sketch is provoking some serious reactions online
body: SNL sketches often go viral, but it's not often they generate quite this much conversation. On Saturday, SNL featured a pre-taped skit called "Sister" a parody ad narrated by a man (this week's host John Mulaney) struggling to find care for his ageing father. SEE ALSO: John Mulaney roasts 'dumbass' Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in 'SNL' monologue: 'No one likes him' "My dad means the world to me," Mulaney says in the sketch. "So when I noticed him start to slow down, I knew I needed to get him the best care possible. I didn't want to put him in a nursing home, but a private health aid could cost thousands a week. I didn't know where to turn. That's when I heard about...Sister. Sister is a live-in, 24/7 elder care provider that is completely free, and also your sister. "Now I don't have to worry about my dad getting the care and attention he needs, because my sister will do it. And I can get back to my life, and the stuff I like to do." Although the sketch made people laugh, it also filled many including people who have found themselves in the situation depicted in the ad with rage. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. title: Vulcan rocket fails during launch, dealing major blow to SpaceX competitors
author: Stephen Clark
body: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket and 40 Amazon Leo broadband satellites fell back to Earth minutes after liftoff Sunday, a crushing setback that will ripple across all sectors of the US space industry. The Vulcan rocket is on contract to launch roughly half of the US military's national security space missions in the next few years, and Sunday's mission was the first of 38 Vulcan launches booked by Amazon to build out its network of broadband Internet satellites aimed at competing with SpaceX's Starlink. Sunday's failure is expected to ground the rocket for an indefinite period of time. Vulcan is no stranger to close calls, having overcome failures with its strap-on solid rocket boosters on two of its four previous flights. In each case, the rocket corrected for those problems and continued into orbit to deploy its payloads. The incidents trigged months-long reviews and investigations before ULA could resume Vulcan flights. Read full article Comments

body: Fanfiction lovers, your global crisis is over. Archive of Our Own (AO3), the popular nonprofit, volunteer-run site for transformative fan works, is back online after a 17-day outage. The site went offline on Oct. 29 following a reported security incident that prompted a wave of maintenance. The Organization for Transformative Works (OTW), which runs AO3, estimated that the maintenance could take up to a month. SEE ALSO: AO3's outage has exposed a growing divide between fanfiction authors and readers That the site is back after just over two weeks is a relief to fandoms all over, especially as the site's outage highlighted a larger divide between fanfiction authors and readers . However, there are still a few key things to know about AO3's earlier-than-expected return. Want more tech and digital culture news delivered to your inbox daily or sent straight to your device? Sign up for Mashable's Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today. AO3 wants you to change your password. In an update about AO3's return , OTW addressed the security incident that caused the outage in the first place. "We will not be sharing specifics about what mitigating changes are being made at this time," the update read. "However, we do want to share that we ve partnered with a security firm to review the incident and analyze the site to help prevent future incidents. AO3's security is deeply important to us." title: John Mulaney roasts dumbass Robert F. Kennedy Jr. in SNL monologue: No one likes him
body: John Mulaney spent a solid chunk of his seventh Saturday Night Live monologue going nuclear on US Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. SEE ALSO: 'SNL's Weekend Update skewers FAA ground stop, Jensen Huang affairs, and more The bit began with Mulaney talking about hosting his children's friends, and how one child always seems to have an old man voice, not unlike Kennedy's. From there, Mulaney launched into a full-on impression of Kennedy, rasping, "Stop the science! Robitussin, when taken during menstruation, will cause telekinesis." Mulaney then talked about how "no one likes [Kennedy] anymore," not even his right-wing friends who used to approve of Kennedy. SEE ALSO: Bowen Yang plays ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in 'SNL' cold open "You dumbass, your thing can't be the measles," Mulaney said. "That can't be your project, giving people the measles." After riffing on Kennedy's poor health track record and his inability to live up to his father's legacy, Mulaney explained that he knew Kennedy during his early days in New York ("He wasn't hard to know"). He skewered everything from his work as an environmental lawyer to his organization Riverkeeper, which was in charge of keeping the Hudson River "whose native fish is tied-off used condom" clean. Mulaney recalled how he and other comedians would perform at the annual Riverkeeper benefit, and how he once received a garbled voicemail from Kennedy thanking him for the performance. While Mulaney described bombing at the benefit, this SNL monologue had the opposite effect. Watch the full set above.

title: SNLs Weekend Update skewers FAA ground stop, Jensen Huang affairs, and more
body: Saturday Night Live 's Weekend Update had a rich array of news stories to tackle this week, from the FAA's nationwide ground stop to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's multiple affairs . Naturally, hosts Michael Che and Colin Jost kicked off the segment by joking about both. SEE ALSO: Bowen Yang plays ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in 'SNL' cold open "The FAA suddenly and mysteriously grounded all US flights yesterday," Jost began. "'Oh thank God, a different news story,' said Jensen Huang." Che and Jost continued to poke fun at the FAA's grounding of all US flights. According to Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy, the ground stop was caused by a maintenance issue involving a switch from copper wire to fiber-optic cable . "So one guy switched out one wire and took out all planes? I think that's literally a scene from the movie Airplane! " Jost continued. Next up, Che and Jost delved into Huang's sex scandal, including his affair with an alleged Chinese spy . "Jensen Huang agreed to testify before Congress about his extramarital affairs," Che said. "Anything to avoid going home." The pair also touched on the economic ramifications of Huang's resignation. "The Jensen Huang sex scandal has sent Nvidia's stock tumbling , which is scaring financial experts since Nvidia's chips are powering the AI boom that is propping up the entire US economy," Jost said. "Which means Jensen Huang had a midlife crisis so bad, you might lose your house in his divorce." title: Elon Musks shares POV footage of Starship after the catch
body: Yesterday was a good day for SpaceX and Elon Musk , and a banner day in the history of man's quest for the stars. Not only did the launch of Starship, the largest interplantery rocket in the SpaceX fleet, standing over 400 feet tall and weighing over 5,000 tons , go off without a hitch from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas, but the vessel successfully delivered its payload of 26 Starlink V3 satellites over the course of its 22.5-hour mission, according to reporting from CNN , while orbiting the Earth 14 times. But the real sticking point was always going to be the landing, where the SpaceX team attempted to prove their "reusable" rocket theory by successfully catching the falling Starship with some well-timed rocket boosters and incredible feats of engineering. The catch has been attempted a few times before on prior missions, successfully for the Super Heavy Booster on three occasions , but yesterday marked the first time the actual Starship was caught by the company's giant mechanical arms. title: Bowen Yang plays ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in SNL cold open
body: This week's news about former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang 's multiple affairs including one with an alleged Chinese spy felt tailor-made for a Saturday Night Live cold open. During last night's episode, hosted by John Mulaney, the show more than delivered. SEE ALSO: A third Jensen Huang affair just dropped The cold open takes place at CIA headquarters, where an officer (Mulaney) has gathered some of the nation's top tech billionaires: Peter Thiel (James Austin Johnson), Sam Altman (Ben Marshall), Dario Amodei (Jane Wickline), Elon Musk (Jeremy Culhane), and Mark Zuckerberg (Andrew Dismukes). The CIA officer has assembled them all to teach them about honey traps, and how not to potentially reveal state secrets to foreign assets, Huang-style. SNL tapped former cast member Bowen Yang to play Huang, or, as he dubs himself in the sketch, Jensen "Hide Your Wives" Huang. Yang also made an appearance in a later sketch: an elaborate musical ode to Central Park, part of the long-running tradition of Mulaney musical sketches. Yang played the "Mary Todd Lincoln Tunnel," a tribute to his current role as Mary Todd Lincoln in Broadway's Oh, Mary! (Yes, he's wearing his costume, along with Mary's signature bratty curls.) To catch Yang's return, as well as some timely digs at the Microsoft Outlook outage and FAA nationwide ground stop , check out the full cold open above.

title: How the world’s fires changed while humanity hit pause
author: Yook Ji Hun
body: Wildfires occur worldwide, and they can sometimes become serious threats to people's lives. A series of massive bushfires from 2019 to 2020 swept across southeastern Australia and destroyed thousands of homes. Recently, the 2025 Los Angeles wildfires spread widely across the city, resulting in massive damage to local communities. Many things can cause wildfires, but humans are the only factor that can also make preventative efforts. Measuring people's impact on fire is difficult because of the mix of human and natural influences. A team led by Jianghao Wang, a professor at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, recently published a study in Cell Reports Sustainability comparing the COVID-19 era with other years. Data from the 2020 lockdowns suggest that lower human activity at this time had the net effect of lowering average fire activity. Read full article Comments

body: There's a little more to see on the Moon tonight as the crescent continues to fill out, so if you're into Moon gazing, grab your viewing gear and head outside. What is today's Moon phase? As of Sunday, Nov. 15, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Crescent phase, with 30% of its surface visible. If you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mare Crisium and the Mare Fecunditatis. With binoculars or a telescope, you'll also see the Endymion Crater, Posidonius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And for keen Moon gazers with a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 11 and 17 landing spots. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on November 24. What are Moon phases? The Moon takes approximately 29.5 days to complete one full cycle. As it orbits Earth, the amount of sunlight reflecting off its surface that we can see changes, creating the different phases. This takes us from the New Moon to the Full Moon and back again, before the cycle begins once more, according to NASA . The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.
